Package dev.relism.flash.testing

Class FlashTest

java.lang.Object
dev.relism.flash.testing.FlashTest
All Implemented Interfaces:
org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.AfterAllCallback, org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.AfterEachCallback, org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.BeforeAllCallback, org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.BeforeEachCallback, org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.Extension
public final class FlashTest extends Object implements org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.BeforeAllCallback, org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.AfterAllCallback, org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.BeforeEachCallback, org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.AfterEachCallback
Runs a real App on an OS-assigned loopback port for a test class or a single test, and gives you a client pointed at it. The app is the one production runs, built by the same code: nothing is reinstalled by hand, and a fake replaces exactly one service. 

 class UserRoutesTest {

     @RegisterExtension
     static FlashTest api = FlashTest.of(() -> Main.api(testDatabase()))
             .replace(Mailer.class, new FakeMailer());

     @Test
     void listsUsers() {
         api.get("/api/users").expectStatus(200).expectBodyContains("alice");
         assertEquals(1, api.services().get(Users.class).count());
     }
 }

Nothing is built or started until first use, so an app that reads a @TempDir sees it populated, and one server can be wired from another in declaration order: 


 @RegisterExtension static FlashTest auth = FlashTest.of(FakeIdentityProvider::app);
 @RegisterExtension static FlashTest api  = FlashTest.of(() -> Main.api(auth.baseUri()));

A static field runs one server for the class; an instance field runs a fresh one for every test — stock JUnit field semantics.

    • of

      public static FlashTest of(Supplier<App> application)
      A harness for the app application builds, when the test first needs it.

    • config

      public FlashTest config(Consumer<ServerConfig.ServerConfigBuilder> config)
      Customises the server: timeouts, HTTP/2 switches, limits. Host, port and the drain window are the harness's, set after this runs; a listener or TLS setting is refused, because the harness owns the one plaintext loopback listener it hands you a client for.
